story.1.title: The World of Aetheria
story.1.body: Since ancient times, Aetheria has run on Code — digital incantations powering machines, bridges, and life itself.
story.2.title: The Glitch Storm
story.2.body: A glitch storm struck Boot Valley. Gates went dark, machines broke, and the engineers lost control.
story.3.title: You Arrive
story.3.body: You are a youth carrying an ancient tool: the ability to PROGRAM. In your hands, code is power.
story.4.title: Begin.
story.4.body: Find Mira in the valley. The world waits to be reignited — by your code.

quest.boot01.obj2: Power the gate via the Code Terminal (loop of 3 pulses)
mira.first.1: Oh! A new visitor in Boot Valley! I'm Mira, bridge engineer.
mira.first.2: The bridge gate over there died completely in yesterday's glitch storm.
mira.first.3: I've set up a Code Terminal near the gate. Go learn the basics first!
mira.first.4: Then we'll make this world respond to YOUR code. See you at the gate!
mira.repeat.1: The Code Terminal is waiting up north. Remember: code is your power here.
mira.turnin.1: I saw the light from here! The gate is glowing… you did it!
mira.turnin.2: You just changed the world with your own code. That's real power, you know?
mira.turnin.3: Thank you! Here's your first reward — an investment in your adventure.
mira.done.1: Boot Valley is safe for now. Your adventure is just beginning!
mira.done.2: Soon there'll be a new tunnel up north — I hear strange machines live there…
sign.boot.text: « Boot Valley — where every code adventure begins. »
course.js_dasar.title: Code Basics
course.js_dasar.desc: Real programming foundations: variables, conditions, and loops — the same language as Aetheria's Code Terminals.
chapter.variabel.title: Variables — Storage Boxes
chapter.kondisi.title: Conditions — Forked Paths
chapter.loop.title: Loops — Repeating Incantations
lesson.apa-itu-variabel.title: What is a Variable?
lesson.jika-dan-lainnya.title: If & Else
lesson.loop-for.title: The for Loop — Repeat with a Counter
b.var.1: In Aetheria, a **variable** is a labeled box where you store things: energy numbers, an adventurer's name, or a secret message.
b.var.2: You create one with `let`, give it a name, then fill it with `=`.
b.var.quiz.q: Which is the CORRECT way to create a variable holding the number 25?
b.var.ex.ins: Complete sapa() so it returns the text "Halo, Aetheria!" — use the sambutan variable.
b.kond.1: Aetheria's gates read conditions: **if** energy is enough → open; **otherwise** → stay locked. In code: `if` and `else`.
b.kond.quiz.q: energi = 10. What does the code above print?
b.kond.quiz.e: 10 >= 25 is false, so the else block runs.
b.kond.ex.ins: Complete cekGerbang(energi): return "buka" if energi >= 25, otherwise "terkunci".
b.loop.1: The bridge gate needs **3 pulses**. Writing bridge.pulse() three times? Works — but programmers use a **loop**.
b.loop.2: Three parts: start (`let i = 0`), continue condition (`i < 3`), and step (`i++`).
b.loop.quiz.q: for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) — how many times does the body run?
b.loop.ex.ins: Complete jumlahDenyut(n): return the total pulses if the loop runs n times — just return n.
b.loop.practice: Time to prove it in the real world: open the Code Terminal near the bridge gate and power it with a 3-pulse loop!
